newsitem.title: UK: Amstrad boosted by reconstruction plan.
newsitem.headline: Amstrad boosted by reconstruction plan.

text.p: Shares in Amstrad Plc were up on Tuesday after the electrical consumer goods company said it was seeking approval for a reconstruction.
By 0750 GMT Amstrad shares were up 7 percent or 18-1/2p to 282p.
"The markets think this will be a good deal", one trader said.
Under the plan, shareholders would receive for each Amstrad share 163p nominal of loan notes exchangeable for cash, a share in the new Viglen Technology and a pro-rata share in Betacom Plc.
An Amstrad spokesman said the Betacom holding should be worth 23-25p per Amstrad share.
Shareholders will also be entitled to the proceeds of litigation which Amstrad is involved in against Seagate Technology Inc and Western Digital Corporation.
Amstrad was last month awarded 57.6 million stg against Seagate and a further hearing will determine interest and costs. Amstrad is seeking a total of 105 million stg gross.
The spokesman said this should be worth 58p per share once the tax has been paid.
Shareholders should therefore receive around 245p per share plus a share in the new Viglen Technology company, the Amstrad spokesman said.

Amstrad chairman Alan Sugar, the founder of the company and chairman of Tottenham Hotspur Plc, is likely to join the board of Viglen as a non-executive director. Sugar has a stake of 34 percent in Amstrad.
